html:
SMTO-GWT-0054 — The Gateway computer didn't answer in time

GUID: b0fe82f5-d6d4-40cb-8131-0b512efd8308
Slug: gateway-connect-timeout
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO tried to connect to the Gateway but heard nothing back before it gave up. The computer may be off or asleep, or a firewall may be silently blocking it. This request was not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the Gateway computer is switched on, not asleep, and connected to the network. A sleeping or disconnected computer simply never answers, which looks exactly like this.
  2. If the Gateway is on a work or private network, make sure the SMTO computer is connected to it, for example that the VPN is on. Traffic sent outside the right network often disappears without any reply.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit, and check that Host and Port are the ones the Gateway's manager gave you. A wrong address can lead to a computer that never answers.
  4. Select Check connection. If it still times out, ask the Gateway computer's manager to check whether a firewall blocks the Gateway's port. Firewalls that drop connections without replying cause this kind of wait.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows the Gateway as connected, and your request runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer or your network. Before repeating an earlier step that was interrupted, check whether it already finished; this timeout doesn't prove earlier work didn't run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Connecting to the selected inbound Gateway failed with ETIMEDOUT before the request was sent; no connection was established within the connect deadline.

What this means

  • Connection setup returned ETIMEDOUT before application transmission, exhausting the connection attempt without establishing a usable socket. This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.

Why this can happen

  • Connection setup returned ETIMEDOUT before application transmission, exhausting the connection attempt without establishing a usable socket.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect endpoint, listener and path reachability; a connection timeout alone cannot distinguish a stopped host from silent network filtering.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the Gateway host is up and the Gateway listens on the configured host and port, and that no firewall or security group silently drops packets from the Server host (timeouts, unlike refusals, usually mean dropped traffic). Test from the Server host with nc -vz host port, then use Check connection.
  • Check the Gateway listener, network reachability and configured endpoint.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A connection to the same intended endpoint completes within its deadline and verifies identity.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
